# Storage map

Every SQLite table CamStack creates, and the file that owns it. There is no
schema file to read — tables come into existence five different ways, so a
map showing only one of them would be worse than none.

**Columns are deliberately not listed here.** They live in the owning file,
which this table points at; duplicating them is how a reference rots. The
pointer stays true through any rename the compiler accepts.

## 1. Canonical key-value collections

A fixed list in `SqliteSettingsBackend`, each `(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data TEXT
NOT NULL)` — the whole record is JSON in `data`.

| Collection |
| --- |
| `system-settings` |
| `addon-settings` |
| `addon-device-settings` |
| `device-runtime-state` |

## 2. Per-addon scoped variants

Any addon writing through `ctx.settings` gets `<addonId>:<canonical>` — for
example `pipeline-analytics:addon-devices`. These are created ON DEMAND at the
first write and are declared nowhere, so **a live hub holds tables that appear
in no source file**. Only the rule is derivable; the list is not. To see the
real set, read `sqlite_master` on the running node.

> This is also the trap behind "the setting saved but the addon never saw it":
> two different tables, both plausible. See the repo's per-device-store note.

columns and indexes. These are the typed, domain-owned tables.

### 3a. Semantic class — what losing a table would cost

A name says nothing about whether losing a table is a bug. The classes are:

| Class | Means | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ledger` | a fact only this component ever held — "the last observation I ACCEPTED" | must be durable; must not be pruned against a fallible read |
| `mirror` | a derived copy of an authority that lives elsewhere | rehydrated from the authority; a persisted copy may only prevent a cold window |
| `ephemeral` | correct to lose | must not be persisted |
| `config` | operator intent | already durable everywhere |
| `audit` | written for a human, never read back by the system | bounded, never a gate |

Declared in a `@durable` annotation on the collection-name constant, which
is the only authority for it — see `scripts/lib/parse-storage.ts`. Any
declared collection without one fails
`scripts/check-durable-state-declared.ts`.

That guard's shrink-only backlog reached **zero on 2026-08-14** — the 44
collections that predated the annotation are all classified, so the table
below is the WHOLE declared surface rather than the part somebody got to.
An unclassified collection can no longer appear here, because it cannot be
committed.

| Collection | Class | Owner | Write trigger | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_record_kinds` | `config` | `records` | an owner declares its kinds when its addon boots (declareKinds): one row per (owner, kind) | none - a kind row is never removed by this release; a kind no installed package declares is only marked orphaned |
| `_record_sequences` | `config` | `records` | allocateId on a kind: one counter row per kind | none - the counter must never go back, so it is never pruned |
| `admin_tokens` | `config` | `local-auth` | none since D895 — the pre-D892 rows are kept on disk, read by nothing | the operator drops the table by hand |
| `auth_audit` | `ledger` | `local-auth` | one row per audited auth event: a second factor skipped from a trusted network, an admin token created / used / revoked, a bulk revoke of credentials | the daily reap deletes rows older than 90 days |
| `backup_encryption_keys` | `config` | `backup-orchestrator` | `setupEncryption` inserts one row per generated key and retires the previous active row; `disableEncryption` retires the active row | none — one small row per key ever generated; a retired row names the key older archives need |
| `calendars:user-prefs` | `config` | `calendars` | `setCalendarPreference` upserts the caller's row | none — a missing row reads as empty prefs (all visible, system colours). Losing the table silently resets every operator's colour/hide choices. |
| `device_credentials` | `config` | `local-auth` | an enrollment completes (QR or self) inserts a row; a renewal rewrites fingerprint/expiry; every accepted certificate login rewrites lastUsedAt/From; an admin revokes or renames | a revoked or long-expired row is kept 90 days for the audit question 'which device was that', then the daily reap deletes it; an active row is never deleted |

Bounded by the fleet an operator configures (974 rows on the reference hub). |
| `keychain:audit` | `audit` | `keychain` | one row per write / delete / rotation / reveal / recovery download | 90 days and at most 20 000 rows, pruned at boot and daily |

| `pipeline-analytics:track-purity` | `ledger` | `pipeline-analytics` | one row per track the operator called `mixed` or `not-a-subject` (`setTrackPurity` / `debug.gt.setPurity`); `pure` deletes it. | NOT track retention and NOT an age clock (D681). Bounded by ROW COUNT (MAX_TRACK_PURITIES, 5 000), oldest `updatedAt` first. |
| `pipeline-analytics:track-relations` | `ledger` | `pipeline-analytics` | one row per unordered pair of tracks the operator related (`setTrackRelation` / `debug.gt.setRelation`); re-marking the pair replaces the row; `clearTrackRelation` deletes it. | NOT track retention and NOT an age clock — ground truth is kept after its tracks are gone (D681). Bounded by ROW COUNT (MAX_TRACK_RELATIONS, 20 000), oldest `updatedAt` first, trimmed on write. |
| `pipeline-analytics:tracking-tapes` | `ledger` | `pipeline-analytics` | one row per PROMOTED tracking-tape window (`debug.tape.promote`); updated when the operator marks it reviewed or releases its pins; deleted together with its file by `debug.tape.delete`. | NOT an age clock and NOT track retention — a promoted window is history being labelled (D681). Bounded by the promotion budget (MAX_PROMOTED_TAPES = 60, 1 GiB): a promotion beyond it is REFUSED, never satisfied by evicting another row. |
| `pipeline-analytics:tracks` | `ledger` | `pipeline-analytics` | one row when a tracked object EXPIRES — persistCompleted upserts at TTL, so an active track lives in RAM only and a restart loses nothing but the tracks still in flight. Plus persistSyntheticTrack for the marker tracks. The row is then UPDATED in place for the tiered label, importance and bestEventId, the retrain status and the operator flags. | THE cascading age root — the track sweep selects on lastSeen per device (trackRetentionDays, or the follow-recordings horizon; default 7 days, 0 = keep forever) and deleting a row pulls its object events, media, face and plate rows and its CLIP vector away with it. Rows with retrainStatus 'staging', favourited, or benchPinned (a promoted tracking-tape window, D681) are PINNED out of the sweep until the operator is done (D81). |
| `recorder:segment-hours` | `mirror` | `recorder` | write-behind on every finalized segment (hour-row upsert, serialised per hour); the writer SEALS the hour it leaves (one write per hour); a listing of a closed hour re-derives the aggregate and seals; eviction and relocation shrink it | a row goes when the walk or eviction confirms the hour is empty — never by age, never from the ledger alone (D148) |
| `records` | `ledger` | `records` | every ctx.records write of an owning addon: one row per record of any declared kind, keyed (kind_id, id) | per kind, declared with the kind: an engine ttl, a row bound, the owner's own sweep, or none - the reason is shown in System -> Data |
| `scoped_tokens` | `config` | `local-auth` | none since D895 — the pre-D892 scoped-token rows are kept on disk, read by nothing (a scoped token is a `credential-tokens` row) | the operator drops the table by hand |
| `storage_drain_state` | `config` | `storage-orchestrator` | one row per location the operator has switched to `drain`, rewritten on every pressure sweep (60 s) while it drains | the row is deleted the moment the location leaves `drain` mode. Bounded by the number of disks a human is retiring at once. |
| `storage_locations` | `config` | `storage-orchestrator` | an operator creates or edits a location (basePath, minFreePercent, enabled, node pin); plus the boot reconcile — declared defaults seeded on a fresh install, and in-memory-only locations backfilled when the store is late-wired | none — a row goes only when the operator deletes the location, or when the declaration pass prunes one whose declaring addon is gone. Bounded by the storage targets a human configures. |
| `user_external_identities` | `config` | `local-auth` | `ExternalIdentityManager.link` when a signed-in user completes a link flow; `unlink` from the profile or the Users page | `unlink` deletes one row; deleting the user deletes all of its rows (`deleteUser` → `removeAllForUser`). A row whose provider instance was renamed or removed stays, inert, until someone unlinks it. |
| `user_totp` | `config` | `local-auth` | `setup` inserts a keychain marker for the user's seed (D878; deleting any pending row first); `confirm` flips `confirmedAt` once a valid code proves possession | `disable` deletes the row, and `setup` deletes before re-inserting. Nothing else prunes — deleting a USER does not cascade here, so their enrollment row outlives the account. |
| `users` | `config` | `local-auth` | an operator creates a user, or `ensureAdminExists` seeds the configured admin on first boot (or resets its password on the operator's one-shot RESET_ADMIN_PASSWORD trigger); updated on scope, isAdmin and password edits | none — a row goes only when an operator deletes the user. A `declareCollection` that adds a PK/UNIQUE/NOT-NULL-without-default column REBUILDS the table: every account is wiped and only the configured admin comes back on the next boot. |
